title: Which digits hide in three more letter addition puzzles?
description: Three letter puzzles with addition are solved from the units column, the way the book's solved example does it. The first needs a carry, the second adds a number three times and has three answers, and the third has a repeated last digit. Each answer is put back into its puzzle to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: start from the units column, decide whether a carry comes in, and use the number of digits in the answer. Watch for students who add the tens column without asking whether a carry came from the units.

source: Digits in Disguise: more addition puzzles
video_script.why: The child has solved one letter sum and now meets puzzles with carries, repeated addition and more than one answer.
video_script.substitution: Work from the units, ask whether a carry happens, and use how many digits the answer has.
video_script.anchor: the three letter addition puzzles of the book: AB + 37 = 6A, ON + ON + ON = PO and QR + QR + QR = PRR
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty five plus thirty seven is sixty two.

final_answer.spoken: twenty five plus thirty seven is sixty two, seventeen, twenty four or thirty one give fifty one, seventy two or ninety three, and eighty five three times is two hundred and fifty five

maths_rules: (i) AB + 37 = 6A: with no carry A + 3 = 6, A = 3, then B + 7 must end in 3, so B + 7 = 13, which carries 1, a contradiction
(i) so a carry of 1 comes in: A + 3 + 1 = 6, A = 2; B + 7 ends in 2, so B + 7 = 12, B = 5; 25 + 37 = 62
(ii) ON + ON + ON = 3 × ON = PO has two digits, so ON is at most 33 and O is 1, 2 or 3; 3 × N ends in O
(ii) O = 1: N = 7, 17 × 3 = 51; O = 2: N = 4, 24 × 3 = 72; O = 3: N = 1, 31 × 3 = 93; the letters O, N, P are different in each
(iii) QR × 3 = PRR; 3 × R ends in R, so R is 0 or 5; R = 0 forces Q = 0, not allowed; R = 5 gives 3 × 5 = 15, carry 1
(iii) 3 × Q + 1 ends in 5, so 3 × Q + 1 = 25, Q = 8, carry 2, P = 2; 85 × 3 = 255; Q = 8, R = 5, P = 2 are different
video_script.design: Three puzzles in order, each solved from the units column with the carry question. The check puts every answer back.

narration: <bookmark mark='nocarry'/>Step one, solve the first puzzle. If no carry came, eigh plus three would be six, so eigh would be three.
<bookmark mark='clash'/>Then B plus seven would need to end in three, which is thirteen, and that does carry one.
<bookmark mark='carry'/>A carry must come in. Then eigh plus three plus one is six, and eigh is two.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Then B plus seven must end in two, which is twelve, so B is five.

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step two, solve the second puzzle. Three times O N has only two digits, so O is one, two or three.
<bookmark mark='units'/>The last digit of the answer is O, so three times N must end in O.
<bookmark mark='one'/>For O as one, N is seven, and seventeen times three is fifty one.
<bookmark mark='two'/>For O as two, N is four, and twenty four times three is seventy two.
<bookmark mark='three'/>For O as three, N is one, and thirty one times three is ninety three.

narration: <bookmark mark='units'/>Step three, solve the third puzzle. Three times R must end in R, so R is zero or five.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>If R were zero, Q would be zero too, and a number cannot start with zero.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Then R is five, and three times five is fifteen, which carries one.
<bookmark mark='q'/>Three times Q plus one must end in five. That is twenty five, so Q is eight and P is two.
